messages:
devon: heads up — CI microbench failed on PR #17901, kv-batcher oscillation. perf-bot attached the job: https://ci.redwood/builds/17901/job/bench-micro-kv
perf-bot: ALERT: microbench/kvcache_throughput regression +18% tail-latency vs baseline (threshold 8%)
aj: ugh, saw that in my local run too. interestingly the regression only shows up on the p4-fast nodes
olga: do we have a bisect hint? any suspect commits in that PR?
devon: my hunch is the batcher hysteresis tweak in the PR — changed backoff from 4->2 cycles to be more aggressive. That interacts with the new kernel selector we merged last week
maria: I can try a local bisect across the two changes (kernel-selector merge + this PR). which commit SHAs?
devon: kernel-selector merge: ab12c3f, PR-17901 branch head: f9e2a1b
stefan: repro command I used: ```
./tools/bench_micro --bench kvcache_throughput --nodes p4-fast --runs 50 --seqdist short
```
aj: repro attached logs: ``[KV] hit_rate=%  drop=0.12 cycles=2 batch_mean=64 kernel=BLAZE_v2`` — you can see hit drops when cycles drop below 3
maria: running bisect now — toggling the hysteresis flag on PR branch to 4 and rerunning a small sample
perf-bot: CI job 17901-try-2 queued on p4-fast (expect ~20m)

(20m pass)

maria: quick update — when I flip cycles back to 4 the local microbench stabilizes, tail-latency back to baseline
devon: that suggests interaction, not purely kernel selector. maybe kernel selector assumes some minimum batch window for amortization
olga: could be KV set churn: aggressive backoff reduces coalescing and increases eviction churn, hurting hot-key paths
stefan: I captured a flame on the failing run — looks like repeated kernel rebinds every 120ms: https://perf.redwood/flames/17901/trace

olga: next steps: 1) reproduce in CI with PR reverted hysteresis tweak, 2) try kernel-selector pinned to pre-merge commit, 3) run longer stability run (500 iters)
aj: agree. I'll open a revert PR for the hysteresis tweak as a hotfix if CI repros
ndevon: typo in username — should be devon: we probably want a canary revert on dedicated to validate before full revert

maria: created revert: https://git.redwood/r/17901/revert-hysteresis, triggered microbench — queued
perf-bot: Revert PR 17901-revert-hyst automatically triggered benchmarks: microbench/kvcache_throughput, microbench/batcher_latency

(10m)

perf-bot: revert run looks green. microbench/kvcache_throughput within baseline (-1%..+2%)
stefan: good signal. aj — do you want to merge revert and follow up with a reduced-change PR?
aj: merging revert now, rolling out patch to canary group. we'll open follow-up to tune backoff with telemetry gates and unit tests for kv-hit-rate
olga: also adding regression unit that simulates hot-key churn with short seqdist so we don't miss this interaction next time
devon: filing bisect notes and root-cause summary: aggressive batcher backoff (cycles=2) reduces batching/coalescing -> increases eviction churn & kernel rebind frequency -> causes throughput oscillation on p4-fast with new kernel selector heuristics. Mitigation: revert, add guardrail, telemetry check, and tweak kernel selector to be robust to shortened batch windows.
maria: adding the summary to the PR and to the perf run ticket: https://tickets.redwood/PR-17901/perf
aj: nice work everyone. follow-up owners: aj (revert + canary), maria (bisect notes + ticket), olga (regression test), stefan (kernel-selector adjustment).
devon: thanks — we should add an alert that triggers when kvcache hit-rate swings >5% post-deploy to catch cross-component interactions earlier :eyes:
perf-bot: NOTE: created perf-alert rule 'kvcache-hit-swing' (threshold=5%)
aj: will try to land the follow-up today. closing thread once revert lands and canary is green
